extracted.intended_audience: research administrators, faculty (especially social sciences & humanities), and university staff who design or run grant-writing supports
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of an ongoing, monthly grant-writing group for faculty/researchers that aims to increase proposal submissions and success; includes program design features, participant-facing practices, and outcome/evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation records (attendance & homework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance records for each meeting, homework submissions to group leaders, and submissions to the internal 'best proposal' competition were used as indicators of the level of sustained participation in the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a proxy for commitment and sustained engagement (e.g., averaged 79% attendance; declines in attendance interpreted as waning momentum). Track session-by-session attendance and homework turn-in rates; note seasonal dips (holidays, conference season).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exit tickets (immediate session feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short anonymous feedback collected at the end of each session asking what went well and what could be improved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to iteratively adapt format and content (e.g., requests for intermingling groups, more examples). Monitor volume and themes of comments (e.g., 25% of comments concerned work-in-progress groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-program participant survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey asking participants to rate how well aspects of process (format, peer feedback time, homework), session characteristics, frequency of experiences (comfort sharing, responsibility), and self-assessed skill changes (nine proposal sections) worked for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Likert scales and categorical yes/no/not sure for skill gains and behavior changes; include open-ended items for qualitative detail. Protect confidentiality with small groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional 'hard' data on submissions and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: University records on grant submissions to internal and external competitions and success (funding awarded) served as objective outcome measures for program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare pre-intervention and post-intervention cycles (e.g., 80% increase in applications; success rate rose from 33% to 50%). Disaggregate by career stage and researcher type (emerging, established, alternative academics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase in number of applications submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric: count of proposals submitted by participants (and at institutional level) before and after the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use percent change across comparable funding cycles (authors report an 80% increase in submissions during/after the group).

rubrics_metrics.name: Success rate in obtaining funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric: proportion of submitted proposals that received funding (internal + external).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate and compare success rates pre/post (example: rose from 33% to 50%); examine differentials across participant subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthened grant-writing skills (specific proposal sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessed strengthening of skills in nine areas required in grant proposals: writing for people outside field; project goals/objectives; statements of significance; outcomes; theoretical frameworks; methodology sections; student training plans; knowledge mobilization/translation plan; budget justifications; and the ability to write an entire grant proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess via yes/no/not sure items per area; use targeted workshops and examples to address weaker areas (e.g., participants wanted more humanities examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of positive writing habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome: participants report having adopted positive new writing habits as a result of participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure as yes/no/not sure; link to homework structure and meeting cadence (e.g., some participants committed to starting proposals earlier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased confidence about applying for grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome: participant self-report of feeling more confident to apply for grants after the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure via survey; correlate with concrete behaviors (submissions) to validate subjective reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manageability of proposal development
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants assess whether group meetings and assignments made developing a grant proposal more manageable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as proximate outcome indicating process improvement and lowered barriers; tie to structure (work-in-progress + mini-lecture + homework).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparedness to give constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome: participant self-assessment that they are better prepared to offer constructive, meaningful feedback on others' proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure via survey; tracks peer-review capacity-building benefits of group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier project initiation behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral metric: likelihood to begin drafting a proposal at least six months before deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as yes/no/not sure; use as indicator of improved planning and time management induced by group structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete production outcome (submitted proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary outcome: whether participation helped develop at least one grant proposal that was submitted in a defined time window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track submission dates and link to participation; useful for attributing tangible outputs to the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant satisfaction and willingness to recommend/repeat
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey items asking whether participants would recommend the group and whether they would participate again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as high-level satisfaction indicators; helpful for program continuation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated ongoing professional contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether participants expect to stay in touch with at least one person met through the group (social, sharing writing, collaboration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures community-building and potential for sustained collaborative benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-in-progress group format
rubrics_metrics.description: Program design: each session begins with small-group work-in-progress discussions where members identify strengths and suggest improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes peer feedback, accountability and commitment. Monitor for anti-patterns (groups that only praise); rotate members or facilitate intermingling to ensure critical feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop + mini-lecture content and handouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Program design: sessions end with a short workshop introducing a new topic and assign homework; provide examples and handouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content to participant needs (budget, knowledge mobilization, student training plans were highly valued). Provide discipline-appropriate examples (humanities needed more). Collect participant requests to guide topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homework assignments and pacing (write sections monthly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured homework: participants were required to write each section of a grant proposal across monthly sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use homework to create momentum and scaffold proposal development; monitor completion rates and provide deadlines tied to meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of time for peer feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocated time within sessions specifically for peer feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveyed as an explicit dimension; ensure enough time is scheduled and enforced to maximize usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator involvement (visiting groups & external sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitators join small groups periodically and accept participants' writing between meetings for feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants valued facilitator visits and outside sharing; facilitators should balance presence to avoid dominating peer review while providing expert guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mock review panels and writing retreats
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities for participants to present completed proposals to mock adjudication committees (e.g., at a writing retreat) for reviewer-style feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simulates adjudication, helps align proposals to reviewer expectations, and provides actionable revision suggestions; schedule retreats near submission timelines and encourage attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of incentives and internal competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing monetary awards (e.g., $5,000 best proposal) and internal competitions to motivate completion and submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can increase participation and submissions but may not overcome last-minute withdrawals; pair awards with structured deadlines and supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing successful proposals and concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Collecting and distributing successful proposals and discipline-appropriate exemplars to participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants requested more humanities examples; use exemplars to teach structure, language and budgeting norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor matchmaking / pairing emerging with established researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Bringing together emerging researchers with established ones to provide mentorship on proposal development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates knowledge transfer and credibility checks; intentionally pair across experience levels for review and coaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional supports & infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational-level strategies that enable proposal success: internal grants, research administrative units, modern facilities, graduate research assistants, and research support services (e.g., computing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement group-level activities; institutional commitment and infrastructure are critical for sustained improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives & workload adjustments as enablers
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific enablers include reduced teaching loads to write applications, salary incentives for successful applications, inclusion of submissions/success in tenure/promotion, travel funds to meet peers/funding agencies, and allocation of discretionary/indirect funds to faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing structural barriers (time and reward) increases likelihood of faculty engaging in grant writing; track policy changes alongside program outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing barriers: time management and familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and mitigate common barriers: time constraints, heavy teaching/service loads, lack of familiarity with budgeting, and lack of awareness of institutional services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scheduled sessions, homework, coaching on budgets, and publicity about services to lower these barriers; monitor differential effects by tenure status and gender as identified in literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social climate: sense of safety, accountability and celebration
rubrics_metrics.description: The social dimension (forming stage, trust, safety) that enables sharing, honest feedback, sustained commitment, and counters negative emotions (anxiety, fear of rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster through consistent meetings, confidentiality norms, celebration of successes, and facilitators modeling constructive critique. Track measures of comfort sharing and feeling safe in surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailoring workshops to disciplinary methodological diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop effectiveness varies by topic and disciplinary diversity (e.g., methodology workshop less effective across diverse humanities/social sciences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer discipline-specific breakout sessions, targeted examples, or curated resources for varied methodologies rather than single omnibus sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation and intermingling of small groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotating group membership or intermingling groups to prevent echo chambers where members focus only on strengths and avoid critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate membership periodically and have facilitators visit groups to ensure critical, constructive feedback and cross-pollination of perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program evaluation design considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixed-methods evaluation using participation records, exit tickets, participant surveys and institutional outcomes; small sample confidentiality considerations limit demographic questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple data sources to triangulate impact; be cautious interpreting causality given self-selection and small n; obtain ethics approval and anonymize responses.
